## Page 1

Mango leaf webber (Orthaga euadrusalis Walker
and O. exvinacea Hampson)
Leaf webbers are
medium sized and
sombre-coloured.
Neonate larvae feed by
scraping chlorophyll
content of leaves.
Second instar larvae
(8-10 no.) cause
webbing the leaves & shoots and feed leaving only the midrib
and veins. Infested cluster of leaves turn dry and brown and
can be noticed from a distance.
Mango mealy bug (Drosicha mangiferae(Green))
Both adult and late
instar nymphs which are
flat, oval shaped
covered with waxy
whitish powder
colonize the bark of tree
trunks. Adult females
and nymphs cause
damage by feeding
tender shoots, flowers and marble sized fruits and cause
shrivelling, drying of young shoots and panicles, reduced size
and premature dropping of fruits. Mealy bugs also secrete
honey dew, favour in
development of sooty
mould.
Thrips (Scirtothrips
dorsalis)
Thrip sare tiny pale yellow
or whitish colour with
numerous dark setae on the body having “fringe” wings.
Thrips colonize and feed fresh leaves, inflorescence and fruits
by lacerating the tissues which results in wilting, drying and
reducing fruit set.They also cause bronzing in mature fruits.w
Mango stem borer
(Batocera sp)
Adults are long, stout dark
beetles measuring 50-60 mm
in length while, neonate grub
feed under the bark
peripherally, larvae bore
deep into the sapwood
making 2-3 cm wide tunnels.
Sticky fluid oozing from
trees, frass exuding from bored hole of tree trunk, yellowing
of branches, drying and dieback of terminal shoots are the
typical symptoms which lead to death of the tree.
Mango fruit fly (Bactrocera sp(Hendel)
Adult flies emerge
during April and lays
6-15 banana shaped
eggs at 1-4 mm deep
in clusters in the
mesocarp by
puncturing skin of
mature fruits. Infested
fruits show small
ovipositional mark on
the skin with ooze
coming out from the
punctured area. Fruit
rots pre-maturely and
become unfit for
consumption with large number of larvae inside the fruit.
M
ango (Mangifera indica L.) is very important
popular fruit of the world and considered as king
of all fruits. Besides delicious taste and excellent
flavour, it is rich in vitamin A&C. In India, mango is cultivated
in an area of 1.23 m ha with the production of 10.99 mt.
Production of mango is enormously handicapped by various
insect pests and diseases from seedling to maturity stage. To
manage the havoc created by these menace, farmers resort to
many rounds of chemical pesticides which leads to
environmental pollution, ecological imbalance, development
of resistance & resurgence, besides leaving harmful residues
in produce.To overcome these problems, Integrated Pest
Management (IPM) strategies must be adopted with chemical
pesticides as a last option to manage the pests in mango.
Mango hoppers (Idioscopus clypealis, I. nitidulus
and Amritodus atkinsoni)
Hoppers have a wedge-shaped body, broad head and narrow
abdomen towards the back with hind legs well adopted for
quick hops. Both nymphs and adults puncture and suck
the sap from
tender shoots,
inflorescences
and leaves, which
cause non-setting
of flowers and
dropping of
immature fruits
which reduce the
crop yield.
Hoppers also
excrete honey
dews which
encourages sooty
mould growth.
Powdery mildew (Oidium mangiferae(Berthet))
White superficial powdery
fungal growth on leaves,
stalks of panicles, flowers
and young fruits are
conspicuous and is
responsible for yield loss
up to 90 per cent. It affects
fruit set and causes fruit
drop.
Mango anthracnose
(Colletotrichum
gloeosporioides)
One of the major pre- and
post-harvest disease of
mango throughout the
world. It infects flowers,
young fruits, leaves, twigs and in the storage mature fruits.
Disease symptoms appear as slightly black sunken irregular
shape lesions which gradually enlarge.
Mango dieback (Lasiodiplodia theobromae)
The disease is characterized
by drying back of
twigs from top downwards,
particularly in older trees
followed by drying of
leaves which gives an
appearance of fire scorch.
Internal browning in wood
tissue is observed when it
is slit open along with the
long axis. Cracks appear on branches and gum exudes before
they die out.

IPM interventions
•Avoid dense planting, prune overcrowded and overlapping
branches. Plough regularly and remove the weeds from
orchard.
•Install yellow and blue sticky traps (50/ha) for hopper
and thrips management.
•Apply entomopathogens like Metarhizium anisopliae and
Beauveria bassiana and botanicals viz., azadirachtin 1%
@ 3 ml/l, lemon grass oil (0.125%) and citronella oil
(0.25%), when the hopper population is low (<4/panicle).
•Apply need based label claim insecticides
viz.,imidacloprid 17.8 SL (0.03%) or thiamethoxam 25
WG (0.05%) for hopper and thrips management.
•Remove leaf webs periodically and destroy for leaf webber
management.
•Flood irrigation of orchard during October kill eggs of
mealy bug.
•Plough the orchard during November-December to expose
different stages of mealy bugs to natural enemies.Remove
nearby alternate weed host, Clerodendrum infortunatum
to reduce infestation.
•Banding tree trunk with alkathene sheet (400 guage) 30
cm above ground level with 25 cm wide and apply grease
from lower end of alkathene which prevents infestation
from crawling nymphs.
•Apply biopesticides like Beauveria bassiana (0.4%) or
5% NSKE around tree trunk during second week of
December.
•Spray Dimethoate 30 EC (0.06%) to manage the nymphs
of mealy bugs ascending on the tree.

Integrated Pest Management of
Mango
D. Raghavendra, P.N. Meena and Subash Chander
ICAR-National Research Centre for Integrated Pest Management
LBS Building, Pusa Campus, New Delhi-110012
•Prune infested branches and remove dead trees infested with
stem borer. Install light traps during May-June to catch adult
borers.
•Remove grubs using wire or hook from the holes of
infested tree trunks and kill. Insert aluminum phosphide
tablets or cotton dipped in petrol and plug with mud
plaster.
•Apply IIHR, Bengaluru formulation “Arka borer control”
on stem from base upto 2.5-3 feet to prevent egg laying
by stem borer (www.iihr.res.in).
•Plough orchard in the month of November – December
to expose fruit fly pupae to sunlight and predators.
•Collect and destroy infested fallen fruits in regular
intervals to reduce fruit fly population.
•Install methyl eugenol traps from reliable source @ 6/
acre during fruiting period from April- August.
•Apply bait splashes on tree trunk and branches with 10%
jaggery + deltamethrin (0.1%) to attract and kill female
fruit flies.
•Immerse mango fruits in hot water at 48°C for 60 min.
within 24 hrs of harvest to kill the eggs without altering
quality.
•Prune plants to facilitate periodically spraying with spray
equipment and improve air circulation in the canopy. Pick
up fallen mango foliage and destroy it. Periodically
remove severely infected panicles. Intercrop mango with
other compatible fruit trees or forestry species. Keep
mango trees weed free to manage powdery mildew.
•Before flowering and immediately after fruit formation spray
need based label claim fungicides,viz., sulphur 80 WP @
0.3% or hexaconazole 5EC @ 0.1% to manage powdery
mildew.
•Remove malformed flowers & paste the cut portion with
Bordeaux mixture. Resort 1% Bordeux mixture or
carbendezim 50 WP @ 0.1% or thiophanate 70 WP @
0.2% to manage mango anthracnose.
•Prune the infected branches and remove dead trees from
the orchard. Apply Blitox 50 WP @ 0.2% for mango
dieback management.
•Conserve natural predators like coccinellids, predatory
thrips, predatory mites, anthocorid bugs, minute pirate
bugs, ground beetles, lacewings, hoverflies and spiders
for hopper and thrips control.
